messages.body_plain:
Hi I'm having some trouble just coloring the branches of a tree that I generated using RAxML.
I have attached 2 files, the bipartitionsBranchLabels to include bootstrapped probabilities as well as the csv containing the list of tips that I would like to highlight.

I understand somewhat of the general approach according to : https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/bioc-ggtree/zjTeAbMQbDg
But I am having trouble implementing whilst including the base RAxML so that I still have access to the bootstrapped values.

GroupOTU colors all the interior edges and every node along the way to the branch which isn't what I want. Just looking to color the individual tips.
A step-by-step breakdown would be the most helpful if someone is available to assist.

Thanks for reading.

Hi all,

Since updating to R v4.0.0 (and ggtree v2.3.0) when using facet_plot if I use xlim_tree to set the limits for my tree panel (as instructed here <https://guangchuangyu.github.io/2016/10/xlim_tree-set-x-axis-limits-for-only-tree-panel/>) or adding a layer to a panel (as here <https://guangchuangyu.github.io/2016/12/add-layer-to-specific-panel-of-facet_plot-output/>) the order of my panels changes.

Recreating the issue using the example here <https://guangchuangyu.github.io/2016/12/add-layer-to-specific-panel-of-facet_plot-output/>, at first everything is plotted as expected:

When I add xlim_tree the order is changed (and also doesn't seem to change the tree limits):

facet_plot(p+xlim_tree(3), panel = 'Stacked Barplot',
           data = df, geom = geom_barh,
           mapping = aes(x = value, fill = category),
           stat='identity' )

The same happens if I add a horizontal line to the bar panel:

mean <- data.frame(x=mean(df$value), .panel='Stacked Barplot')

facet_plot(p, panel = 'Stacked Barplot',
           data = df, geom = geom_barh,
           mapping = aes(x = value, fill = category),
           stat='identity' )  +
  geom_vline(data=mean,
             color="black",
             linetype="dashed",
             aes(xintercept=x))

Is anybody else experiencing this problem or is something going on at my end?

Thanks,

Rowena

gg <- ggtree(phy)

gg %<+% table +
  geom_tiplab() +
  geom_label(aes(x=branch, label=dNdS_values),
                            fill="white",
                            size=2.8,
                            vjust=-1,
                            label.size=0)

Hope it helps!

Rowena

messages.body_plain:
full_join supports both phylo and tbl_tree objects.

The problem here is the user try to merge a tree with annotation data using labels that are not unique to corresponding nodes.
> tail(metadata)
# A tibble: 6 x 2
  label  dN_vs_dS
  <chr>  <chr>
1 "99.8" 0.097*
2 ""     NA
3 "100"  0.0026*
4 "73.1" NA
5 "100"  NA
6 "100"  NA

As we can see that there are multiple “100”, the full_join will try to keep all these possibilities.
> tree

Phylogenetic tree with 12 tips and 11 internal nodes.

Tip labels:
    SP1, SP2, SP3, SP4, SP5, SP6, ...
Node labels:
    Root, 71.5, 87.6, 40.4, 100, 99.8, ...

Rooted; includes branch lengths.
> y
'treedata' S4 object'.

...@ phylo:
Phylogenetic tree with 12 tips and 23 internal nodes.

Tip labels:
    SP1, SP2, SP3, SP4, SP5, SP6, ...
Node labels:
    Root, 71.5, 87.6, 40.4, 100, 100, ...

Unrooted; includes branch lengths.

with the following features available:
    'dN_vs_dS'.
>

The internal node number of the original tree is 11 while in y is 23. The tree in y is not in correct structure. This is the reason the ggtree crash.

If you can make sure that the labels are unique to each node, please use internal node number in the metadata instead of label.

As we can see that there are multiple “100”, the full_join will try to keep all these possibilities.
> tree

Phylogenetic tree with 12 tips and 11 internal nodes.

Tip labels:
    SP1, SP2, SP3, SP4, SP5, SP6, ...
Node labels:
    Root, 71.5, 87.6, 40.4, 100, 99.8, ...

Rooted; includes branch lengths.
> y
'treedata' S4 object'.

...@ phylo:
Phylogenetic tree with 12 tips and 23 internal nodes.

Tip labels:
    SP1, SP2, SP3, SP4, SP5, SP6, ...
Node labels:
    Root, 71.5, 87.6, 40.4, 100, 100, ...

Unrooted; includes branch lengths.

with the following features available:
    'dN_vs_dS'.
>

The internal node number of the original tree is 11 while in y is 23. The tree in y is not in correct structure. This is the reason the ggtree crash.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would like to plot bootstrap values on the nodes of a circular tree but I haven't been able to get geom_nodelab2 to work as I expected.

Below is some example code to produce a normal tree with node labels, a circular tree with node labels using geom_nodelab2 and a manual work around using geom_text2.

Am I using geom_nodelab2 incorrectly? If not, is there a more eloquent way of doing this?

Best wishes
Ollie

# generate tree
set.seed(1234)
tree <- rtree(n=10)

# plot as normal tree with node labels
p <- ggtree(tree)

p + geom_tiplab(aes(label=label)) +
  geom_nodelab(aes(label=node))

# plot as circular tree with node labels
p2 <- ggtree(tree, layout="circular")

# node labels not shown as expected here
p2 + geom_tiplab2(aes(label=label)) +
  geom_nodelab2(aes(label=node))

# node label upside down on left hand side
p2 + geom_text2(aes(label=node, angle=angle))

# manually adjust the angle values
p2$data [ p2$data$angle > 90 & p2$data$angle < 180 , ]$angle   <- p2$data [ p2$data$angle > 90 & p2$data$angle < 180 , ]$angle + 180
p2$data [ p2$data$angle > 180 & p2$data$angle < 270 , ]$angle  <- p2$data [ p2$data$angle > 180 & p2$data$angle < 270 , ]$angle - 180

# as expected
p2 + geom_text2(aes(label=node, angle=angle))
